articles.title: Bonsai Drift Circuit
articles.summary: Faint bonsai branch flow and circuit linework with moss-copper traces; very low contrast, subtle organic sheen. Reads as a clean sheen; the hairlines vanish and only a faint organic scratch character may remain.
articles.what: Reference-backed Rising Sun Spec overlay - bonsai branch flow, nature circuit linework, moss greens, copper traces, and circular brush currents remapped into dynamic M/R/ Up close: Hair-thin meandering lines, like fine wires, roots or traces, wandering mostly vertically with a few small loops and branches. They are bright inside the highlight and dark in the shadow area; the rest of the surface is smooth. From a distance: Reads as a clean sheen; the hairlines vanish and only a faint organic scratch character may remain. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Rising Sun Spec (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: hood, roof, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Rising Sun Spec", or search for "Bonsai Drift Circuit".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic base so veins show in the highlight
Sides where light rakes across
Hairlines do not disturb numbers.
Barely there: a few faint wisps
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not green or copper colour: the moss and copper are only names, the spec adds no colour
Not lightning or crack paint: lines are hair-fine and meandering, not branching forks
Avoid: high-contrast bases that erase the faint lines, cluttered liveries.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
